sanskrit: kasmād ayaṃ rāmajanārdanau ca; pradyumnasāmbau ca mayā sametau vasaty araṇye saha sodarīyais; trailokyanāthān adhigamya nāthān
english: Why do Rāma and Janārdana, along with Pradyumna and Sāmba, who have reached the lords of the three worlds—why do they dwell in the forest together with their kinsmen, though they have found such protectors?

sanskrit: niryātu sādhv adya daśārhasenā; prabhūtanānāyudhacitravarmā yamakṣayaṃ gacchatu dhārtarāṣṭraḥ; sabāndhavo vṛṣṇibalābhibhūtaḥ
english: Let the army of the Dāśārhas march out today, well-armed with many weapons and fine armour. Let the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra go to the abode of Yama, overwhelmed by the might of the Vṛṣṇis, together with all his kinsmen.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hy eva kopāt pṛthivīm apīmāṃ; saṃveṣṭayes tiṣṭhatu śārṅgadhanvā sa dhārtarāṣṭraṃ jahi sānubandhaṃ; vṛtraṃ yathā devapatir mahendraḥ
english: You alone in your wrath could wrap up even this whole earth; let the bearer of the Śārṅga bow stand firm. Slay that son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra along with all his followers, just as the lord of the gods, great Indra, slew Vṛtra.

sanskrit: bhrātā ca me yaś ca sakhā guruś ca; janārdanasyātmasamaś ca pārthaḥ yadartham abhyudyatam uttamaṃ tat; karoti karmāgryam apāraṇīyam
english: He who is my brother, my friend, and my teacher—Pārtha, who is regarded as Janārdana's very self—for his sake the foremost deed, impossible to accomplish, is being undertaken.

sanskrit: tasyāstravarṣāṇy aham uttamāstrair; vihatya sarvāṇi raṇe 'bhibhūya kāyāc chiraḥ sarpaviṣāgnikalpaiḥ; śarottamair unmathitāsmi rāma
english: I shall repel his showers of weapons with my finest missiles in battle, overwhelming them all; yet from his body, with his best arrows that blaze like serpent-venom and fire, I have been utterly shattered, O Rāma.

sanskrit: khaḍgena cāhaṃ niśitena saṃkhye; kāyāc chiras tasya balāt pramathya tato 'sya sarvān anugān haniṣye; duryodhanaṃ cāpi kurūṃś ca sarvān
english: With my sharpened sword in battle I shall forcibly cut off his head from his body, and then I shall slay all his followers, Duryodhana, and all the Kurus.

sanskrit: āttāyudhaṃ mām iha rauhiṇeya; paśyantu bhaumā yudhi jātaharṣāḥ nighnantam ekaṃ kuruyodhamukhyān; kāle mahākakṣam ivāntakāgniḥ
english: Let the people of this earth watch me here, O son of Rohiṇī, weapons in hand, rejoicing in battle as I single-handedly strike down the foremost Kuru warriors in due season, like the fire of death consuming a great heap of dry grass.

sanskrit: pradyumnamuktān niśitān na śaktāḥ; soḍhuṃ kṛpadroṇavikarṇakarṇāḥ jānāmi vīryaṃ ca tavātmajasya; kārṣṇir bhavaty eṣa yathā raṇasthaḥ
english: Kṛpa, Droṇa, Vikarṇa, and Karṇa are not able to withstand the sharp arrows released by Pradyumna. I know well the valour of your son—this son of Kṛṣṇa is formidable when he stands on the battlefield.

sanskrit: sāmbaḥ sasūtaṃ sarathaṃ bhujābhyāṃ; duḥśāsanaṃ śāstu balāt pramathya na vidyate jāmbavatīsutasya; raṇe 'viṣahyaṃ hi raṇotkaṭasya
english: May Sāmba, forcibly seizing Duḥśāsana along with his charioteer and chariot in his two arms, punish him. For nothing in battle is unbearable for the son of Jāmbavatī, that fierce warrior.

sanskrit: etena bālena hi śambarasya; daityasya sainyaṃ sahasā praṇunnam vṛttorur atyāyatapīnabāhur; etena saṃkhye nihato 'śvacakraḥ ko nāma sāmbasya raṇe manuṣyo; gatvāntaraṃ vai bhujayor dhareta
english: By this young hero the army of the demon Śambara was swiftly routed—he of the rounded thighs and exceptionally long, full arms. By him in battle was Aśvacakra slain. What man in battle could enter the gap between Sāmba's arms and survive?

sanskrit: yathā praviśyāntaram antakasya; kāle manuṣyo na viniṣkrameta tathā praviśyāntaram asya saṃkhye; ko nāma jīvan punar āvrajeta
english: Just as a man who enters the jaws of Death at the appointed time does not come out again, so who, having entered the gap between his arms in battle, could return alive?

sanskrit: droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca mahārathau tau; sutair vṛtaṃ cāpy atha somadattam sarvāṇi sainyāni ca vāsudevaḥ; pradhakṣyate sāyakavahnijālaiḥ
english: And Vāsudeva will burn Droṇa and Bhīṣma, those two great chariot-warriors, Somadatta surrounded by his sons, and all the armies, with his net of blazing arrows.

sanskrit: kiṃ nāma lokeṣv aviṣahyam asti; kṛṣṇasya sarveṣu sadaivateṣu āttāyudhasyottamabāṇapāṇeś; cakrāyudhasyāpratimasya yuddhe
english: What in all the worlds, even among the gods, is unbearable for Kṛṣṇa, who has taken up his weapon, whose hands hold the finest arrows, who wields the discus as his weapon, and who is incomparable in battle?

sanskrit: tato 'niruddho 'py asicarmapāṇir; mahīm imāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrair visaṃjñaiḥ hṛtottamāṅgair nihataiḥ karotu; kīrṇāṃ kuśair vedim ivādhvareṣu
english: Then let Aniruddha too, sword and shield in hand, strew this earth with the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra—senseless, their heads severed, slain—as an altar at a sacrifice is strewn with sacred grass.

sanskrit: gadolmukau bāhukabhānunīthāḥ; śūraś ca saṃkhye niśaṭhaḥ kumāraḥ raṇotkaṭau sāraṇacārudeṣṇau; kulocitaṃ viprathayantu karma
english: Bāhuka, Bhānu, and Nītha bearing clubs and fire-brands, the young hero Niśaṭha who is fierce in battle, the war-eager Sāraṇa and Cārudeṣṇa—let them all spread the deeds befitting their noble lineage.

sanskrit: savṛṣṇibhojāndhakayodhamukhyā; samāgatā kṣatriyaśūrasenā hatvā raṇe tān dhṛtarāṣṭraputrāṃl; loke yaśaḥ sphītam upākarotu
english: The assembled army of Kṣatriya heroes, with the foremost warriors of the Vṛṣṇis, Bhojas, and Andhakas, shall win wide fame in the world by slaying the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in battle.

sanskrit: tato 'bhimanyuḥ pṛthivīṃ praśāstu; yāvad vrataṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pārayate mahātmā; dyūte yathoktaṃ kurusattamena
english: Then let Abhimanyu rule the earth while the great-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, foremost among upholders of dharma, fulfils the vow in exile as declared at the dice-game by that best of Kurus.

sanskrit: asmatpramuktair viśikhair jitāris; tato mahīṃ bhokṣyati dharmarājaḥ nirdhārtarāṣṭrāṃ hatasūtaputrām; etad dhi naḥ kṛtyatamaṃ yaśaśyam
english: With enemies conquered by the arrows we release, Dharmarāja shall then enjoy the earth, rid of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the slain son of the sūta. This is indeed our most glorious duty.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca asaṃśayaṃ mādhava satyam etad; gṛhṇīma te vākyam adīnasattva svābhyāṃ bhujābhyām ajitāṃ tu bhūmiṃ; necchet kurūṇām ṛṣabhaḥ kathaṃ cit
english: Vāsudeva said: Without doubt, O Mādhava, this is true; we accept your words, O you of undaunted spirit. But the bull of the Kurus does not wish the earth that is yet unconquered by his own two arms, under any circumstances.

sanskrit: na hy eṣa kāmān na bhayān na lobhād; yudhiṣṭhiro jātu jahyāt svadharmam bhīmārjunau cātirathau yamau vā; tathaiva kṛṣṇā drupadātmajeyam
english: For Yudhiṣṭhira would never abandon his own dharma out of desire, fear, or greed—nor would Bhīma and Arjuna, those two great chariot-warriors, nor the twins, nor indeed Kṛṣṇā, daughter of Drupada.

sanskrit: ubhau hi yuddhe 'pratimau pṛthivyāṃ; vṛkodaraś caiva dhanaṃjayaś ca kasmān na kṛtsnāṃ pṛthivīṃ praśāsen; mādrīsutābhyāṃ ca puraskṛto 'yam
english: For both Vṛkodara and Dhanaṃjaya are peerless in battle on this earth. Why should he not rule the entire earth, he who is accompanied by the two sons of Mādrī?

sanskrit: yadā tu pāñcālapatir mahātmā; sakekayaś cedipatir vayaṃ ca yotsyāma vikramya parāṃs tadā vai; suyodhanas tyakṣyati jīvalokam
english: But when the great-souled lord of the Pāñcālas, together with the king of the Kekayas, the king of the Cedis, and ourselves, shall fight, advancing against the foe—then indeed Suyodhana shall quit the world of the living.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca naitac citraṃ mādhava yad bravīṣi; satyaṃ tu me rakṣyatamaṃ na rājyam kṛṣṇas tu māṃ veda yathāvad ekaḥ; kṛṣṇaṃ ca vedāham atho yathāvat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What you say, O Mādhava, is not surprising; but truth is what I must guard above all, not a kingdom. Kṛṣṇa alone knows me truly, and I know Kṛṣṇa truly.

sanskrit: yadaiva kālaṃ puruṣapravīro; vetsyaty ayaṃ mādhava vikramasya tadā raṇe tvaṃ ca śinipravīra; suyodhanaṃ jeṣyasi keśavaś ca
english: When this foremost of men shall know the right time for valour, O Mādhava, then in battle you, O foremost of Śini's line, and Keśava shall conquer Suyodhana.

sanskrit: pratiprayāntv adya daśārhavīrā; dṛḍho 'smi nāthair naralokanāthaiḥ dharme 'pramādaṃ kurutāprameyā; draṣṭāsmi bhūyaḥ sukhinaḥ sametān
english: Let the Dāśārha heroes depart today. I am steadfast with these lords, lords of the world of men. O you of immeasurable greatness, be not negligent in dharma; I shall see you again, united and happy.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te 'nyonyam āmantrya tathābhivādya; vṛddhān parisvajya śiśūṃś ca sarvān yadupravīrāḥ svagṛhāṇi jagmū; rājāpi tīrthāny anusaṃcacāra
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having taken leave of one another and exchanged salutations, having embraced the elders and all the children, the foremost heroes of the Yadus departed for their own homes; and the king too continued visiting the sacred tīrthas.

sanskrit: visṛjya kṛṣṇaṃ tv atha dharmarājo; vidarbharājopacitāṃ sutīrthām sutena somena vimiśritodāṃ; tataḥ payoṣṇīṃ prati sa hy uvāsa
english: Having bid farewell to Kṛṣṇa, the Dharmarāja then came to the Payoṣṇī, that holy river with its excellent fords, honoured by the king of Vidarbha, its waters mingled with the sacred soma pressed by his son; and there he dwelt.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca nṛgeṇa yajamānena someneha puraṃdaraḥ tarpitaḥ śrūyate rājan sa tṛpto madam abhyagāt
english: Lomaśa said: It is heard, O king, that here the smasher of citadels, Indra, was satisfied with soma by the sacrificer Nṛga, and being satisfied he became intoxicated with delight.

sanskrit: iha devaiḥ sahendrair hi prajāpatibhir eva ca iṣṭaṃ bahuvidhair yajñair mahadbhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ
english: Here indeed, together with Indra and the gods and the lords of creatures, great sacrifices of many kinds were performed with abundant sacrificial fees.

sanskrit: āmūrtarayasaś ceha rājā vajradharaṃ prabhum tarpayām āsa somena hayamedheṣu saptasu
english: And here King Āmūrtarayas satisfied the lord who bears the thunderbolt with soma at seven horse-sacrifices.

sanskrit: tasya saptasu yajñeṣu sarvam āsīd dhiraṇmayam vānaspatyaṃ ca bhaumaṃ ca yad dravyaṃ niyataṃ makhe
english: In his seven sacrifices, all that was appointed for the rite—whether of forest origin or of the earth—was made entirely of gold.

sanskrit: teṣv eva cāsya yajñeṣu prayogāḥ sapta viśrutāḥ saptaikaikasya yūpasya caṣālāś copari sthitāḥ
english: In those very sacrifices of his, seven celebrated rites took place; and on each single sacrificial post seven carved wooden rings were placed above.

sanskrit: tasya sma yūpān yajñeṣu bhrājamānān hiraṇmayān svayam utthāpayām āsur devāḥ sendrā yudhiṣṭhira
english: In those sacrifices of his, the gods together with Indra themselves raised up the gleaming golden sacrificial posts, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: teṣu tasya makhāgryeṣu gayasya pṛthivīpateḥ amādyad indraḥ somena dakṣiṇābhir dvijātayaḥ
english: In those foremost sacrifices of Gaya, the lord of the earth, Indra became intoxicated with soma and the twice-born became intoxicated with the sacrificial fees.

sanskrit: sikatā vā yathā loke yathā vā divi tārakāḥ yathā vā varṣato dhārā asaṃkhyeyāś ca kena cit
english: As the grains of sand in the world, as the stars in the sky, as the streams of falling rain—none of these can be counted by anyone—

sanskrit: tathaiva tad asaṃkhyeyaṃ dhanaṃ yat pradadau gayaḥ sadasyebhyo mahārāja teṣu yajñeṣu saptasu
english: just so was that wealth which Gaya distributed to the participants at those seven sacrifices beyond all counting, O great king.

sanskrit: bhavet saṃkhyeyam etad vai yad etat parikīrtitam na sā śakyā tu saṃkhyātuṃ dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇāvataḥ
english: What has been enumerated here might indeed be counted; but the sacrificial fees of that generous giver cannot be counted.

sanskrit: hiraṇmayībhir gobhiś ca kṛtābhir viśvakarmaṇā brāhmaṇāṃs tarpayām āsa nānādigbhyaḥ samāgatān
english: With golden cows fashioned by Viśvakarman he satisfied the brāhmaṇas gathered from all directions.

sanskrit: alpāvaśeṣā pṛthivī caityair āsīn mahātmanaḥ gayasya yajamānasya tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: The earth had but few sacred shrines left unadorned by the great-souled sacrificer Gaya here and there, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: sa lokān prāptavān aindrān karmaṇā tena bhārata salokatāṃ tasya gacchet payoṣṇyāṃ ya upaspṛśet
english: By that deed he attained the worlds of Indra, O Bhārata; whoever bathes in the Payoṣṇī will attain the same world as Gaya.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam atra rājendra bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'nagha upaspṛśya mahīpāla dhūtapāpmā bhaviṣyasi
english: Therefore, O king of kings, O sinless protector of the earth, you along with your brothers should bathe here and you shall be cleansed of all sin.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa payoṣṇyāṃ naraśreṣṭhaḥ snātvā vai bhrātṛbhiḥ saha vaiḍūryaparvataṃ caiva narmadāṃ ca mahānadīm samājagāma tejasvī bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'naghaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having bathed in the Payoṣṇī with his brothers, that best of men, the radiant and sinless one, proceeded along with his brothers to Mount Vaidūrya and the great river Narmadā.

sanskrit: tato 'sya sarvāṇy ācakhyau lomaśo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ tīrthāni ramaṇīyāni tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: There the venerable sage Lomaśa described to him all the charming sacred fords here and there, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: yathāyogaṃ yathāprīti prayayau bhrātṛbhiḥ saha dadamāno 'sakṛd vittaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: As was proper and as inclination led, he journeyed with his brothers, repeatedly giving wealth by the thousands to brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca devānām eti kaunteya tathā rājñāṃ salokatām vaiḍūryaparvataṃ dṛṣṭvā narmadām avatīrya ca
english: Lomaśa said: One attains the same world as the gods and also as kings, O son of Kuntī, by seeing Mount Vaidūrya and descending into the Narmadā.

sanskrit: saṃdhir eṣa naraśreṣṭha tretāyā dvāparasya ca etam āsādya kaunteya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: This is the junction of the Tretā and Dvāpara ages, O best of men; by reaching this place, O son of Kuntī, one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: eṣa śaryātiyajñasya deśas tāta prakāśate sākṣād yatrāpibat somam aśvibhyāṃ saha kauśikaḥ
english: This is the place of Śaryāti's sacrifice that shines forth, my dear; here Kauśika directly drank soma together with the Aśvins.

sanskrit: cukopa bhārgavaś cāpi mahendrasya mahātapāḥ saṃstambhayām āsa ca taṃ vāsavaṃ cyavanaḥ prabhuḥ sukanyāṃ cāpi bhāryāṃ sa rājaputrīm ivāptavān
english: The great Bhārgava, mighty in austerity, also became angry with great Indra; the powerful Cyavana paralyzed Vāsava, and he also won Sukanyā as his wife, as if she were a princess.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ viṣṭambhitas tena bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ kimarthaṃ bhārgavaś cāpi kopaṃ cakre mahātapāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was the blessed chastiser of Pāka paralyzed by him? And why did that Bhārgava of great austerity become angry?

sanskrit: nāsatyau ca kathaṃ brahman kṛtavān somapīthinau etat sarvaṃ yathāvṛttam ākhyātu bhagavān mama
english: And how did he make the two Nāsatyas drinkers of soma, O brahman? Let the venerable one tell me all of this exactly as it happened.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca bhṛgor maharṣeḥ putro 'bhūc cyavano nāma bhārgavaḥ samīpe sarasaḥ so 'sya tapas tepe mahādyutiḥ
english: Lomaśa said: The son of the great seer Bhṛgu was Cyavana, a Bhārgava; full of great splendour, he performed austerity near a lake.

sanskrit: sthāṇubhūto mahātejā vīrasthānena pāṇḍava atiṣṭhat subahūn kālān ekadeśe viśāṃ pate
english: Standing motionless like a post, full of great energy, O Pāṇḍava, he stood for very many ages in one place, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: sa valmīko 'bhavad ṛṣir latābhir abhisaṃvṛtaḥ kālena mahatā rājan samākīrṇaḥ pipīlikaiḥ
english: The sage became an anthill, covered over with creepers; in the course of a great length of time, O king, he was filled with ants.

sanskrit: tathā sa saṃvṛto dhīmān mṛtpiṇḍa iva sarvaśaḥ tapyati sma tapo rājan valmīkena samāvṛtaḥ
english: Thus covered over, the wise one looked in every way like a lump of clay; yet he performed austerity, O king, enclosed within the anthill.

sanskrit: atha dīrghasya kālasya śaryātir nāma pārthivaḥ ājagāma saro ramyaṃ vihartum idam uttamam
english: Then, after a long time, a king named Śaryāti came to this delightful, excellent lake for recreation.

sanskrit: tasya strīṇāṃ sahasrāṇi catvāry āsan parigrahaḥ ekaiva ca sutā śubhrā sukanyā nāma bhārata
english: He had four thousand women as his retinue, and one fair daughter named Sukanyā, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sā sakhībhiḥ parivṛtā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā caṅkramyamāṇā valmīkaṃ bhārgavasya samāsadat
english: She, surrounded by her companions and adorned with all ornaments, while wandering about came upon the anthill of the Bhārgava.

sanskrit: sā caiva sudatī tatra paśyamānā manoramān vanaspatīn vicinvantī vijahāra sakhīvṛtā
english: That fair-toothed one sported there with her companions, gazing at the charming forest trees and gathering flowers.

sanskrit: rūpeṇa vayasā caiva madanena madena ca babhañja vanavṛkṣāṇāṃ śākhāḥ paramapuṣpitāḥ
english: Drunk with beauty, youth, desire, and pride, she broke off the supremely flowering branches of the forest trees.

sanskrit: tāṃ sakhīrahitām ekām ekavastrām alaṃkṛtām dadarśa bhārgavo dhīmāṃś carantīm iva vidyutam
english: The wise Bhārgava saw her, alone without her companions, clad in a single garment, adorned with jewels, moving like a flash of lightning.

sanskrit: tāṃ paśyamāno vijane sa reme paramadyutiḥ kṣāmakaṇṭhaś ca brahmarṣis tapobalasamanvitaḥ tām ābabhāṣe kalyāṇīṃ sā cāsya na śṛṇoti vai
english: Watching her in the solitude, he of supreme radiance was pleased; the brahmarṣi with emaciated throat, endowed with the power of austerity, spoke to that lovely one—but she did not hear him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sukanyā valmīke dṛṣṭvā bhārgavacakṣuṣī kautūhalāt kaṇṭakena buddhimohabalātkṛtā
english: Then Sukanyā, seeing the eyes of the Bhārgava shining in the anthill, overcome by curiosity and a confusion of mind, took a thorn—

sanskrit: kiṃ nu khalv idam ity uktvā nirbibhedāsya locane akrudhyat sa tayā viddhe netre paramamanyumān tataḥ śaryātisainyasya śakṛnmūtraṃ samāvṛṇot
english: saying "What indeed is this?" she pierced his eyes. He became furious when his eyes were pierced by her, filled with supreme wrath; thereupon he caused the army of Śaryāti to be obstructed in their excretion and urination.

sanskrit: tato ruddhe śakṛnmūtre sainyam ānāhaduḥkhitam tathāgatam abhiprekṣya paryapṛcchat sa pārthivaḥ
english: Then, with excretion and urination blocked, the army suffering from the obstruction—seeing them in such a state, the king asked them about it.

sanskrit: taponityasya vṛddhasya roṣaṇasya viśeṣataḥ kenāpakṛtam adyeha bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ jñātaṃ vā yadi vājñātaṃ tad ṛtaṃ brūta māciram
english: "Who today has done wrong here to the great-souled Bhārgava, who is ever devoted to austerity, who is old, and who is especially irascible? Tell me the truth at once, whether it was done knowingly or unknowingly."

sanskrit: tam ūcuḥ sainikāḥ sarve na vidmo 'pakṛtaṃ vayam sarvopāyair yathākāmaṃ bhavāṃs tad adhigacchatu
english: All the soldiers said to him: "We do not know of any wrong done by us; by all means and as you please, may Your Highness find that out."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pṛthivīpālaḥ sāmnā cogreṇa ca svayam paryapṛcchat suhṛdvargaṃ pratyajānan na caiva te
english: Then that guardian of the earth, with gentle and also severe questioning, himself asked his circle of friends; but they too did not know.

sanskrit: ānāhārtaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā tat sainyam asukhārditam pitaraṃ duḥkhitaṃ cāpi sukanyedam athābravīt
english: Then, seeing the army afflicted with the obstruction and the suffering, and her father in distress, Sukanyā said this:

sanskrit: mayāṭantyeha valmīke dṛṣṭaṃ sattvam abhijvalat khadyotavad abhijñātaṃ tan mayā viddham antikāt
english: "While I was roaming here I saw in the anthill a blazing being, recognised by me like a firefly; that one was pierced by me from close by."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu śaryātir valmīkaṃ tūrṇam ādravat tatrāpaśyat tapovṛddhaṃ vayovṛddhaṃ ca bhārgavam
english: Hearing this, Śaryāti swiftly ran to the anthill; there he saw the Bhārgava, great in austerity and great in age.

sanskrit: ayācad atha sainyārthaṃ prāñjaliḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ ajñānād bālayā yat te kṛtaṃ tat kṣantum arhasi
english: Then with folded hands the lord of the earth besought him for his army's sake: "What was done to you by a young girl in ignorance—that you ought to forgive."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahīpālaṃ cyavano bhārgavas tadā rūpaudāryasamāyuktāṃ lobhamohabalātkṛtām
english: Then Cyavana the Bhārgava spoke to that guardian of the earth, saying of her who was endowed with beauty and nobility, overcome by the force of greed and delusion:

sanskrit: tām eva pratigṛhyāhaṃ rājan duhitaraṃ tava kṣamiṣyāmi mahīpāla satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "Upon receiving her, your daughter, for myself, O king, I will forgive—O guardian of the earth, I tell you this truthfully."

sanskrit: ṛṣer vacanam ājñāya śaryātir avicārayan dadau duhitaraṃ tasmai cyavanāya mahātmane
english: Comprehending the words of the seer, Śaryāti, without deliberation, gave his daughter to that great-souled Cyavana.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ kanyāṃ cyavanaḥ prasasāda ha prāptaprasādo rājā sa sasainyaḥ punar āvrajat
english: And having received that maiden, Cyavana became pleased; the king, having obtained his grace, departed again with his army.

sanskrit: sukanyāpi patiṃ labdhvā tapasvinam aninditā nityaṃ paryacarat prītyā tapasā niyamena ca
english: Sukanyā too, having obtained that austere man as her husband, blameless one, constantly attended upon him with devotion, austerity, and self-discipline.

sanskrit: agnīnām atithīnāṃ ca śuśrūṣur anasūyikā samārādhayata kṣipraṃ cyavanaṃ sā śubhānanā
english: That fair-faced one, devoted to the sacred fires and to guests, free from envy, quickly pleased Cyavana.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca kasya cit tv atha kālasya surāṇām aśvinau nṛpa kṛtābhiṣekāṃ vivṛtāṃ sukanyāṃ tām apaśyatām
english: Lomaśa said: Then, after some time had passed, O king, the two Aśvins among the gods saw Sukanyā as she had bathed, her garments loose and open.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā darśanīyāṅgīṃ devarājasutām iva ūcatuḥ samabhidrutya nāsatyāv aśvināv idam
english: Seeing her of beautiful limbs, like the daughter of a king of the gods, the two Nāsatyas, the Aśvins, approached her swiftly and said this:

sanskrit: kasya tvam asi vāmoru kiṃ vane vai karoṣi ca icchāva bhadre jñātuṃ tvāṃ tat tvam ākhyāhi śobhane
english: "Whose are you, O fair-thighed one, and what are you doing in the forest? We two wish to know about you, O auspicious one—tell us about yourself, O beautiful one."
